description: This file defines the class `SugarJobQueue`, which manages scheduling, submission, retrieval, and cleanup of scheduled jobs in the SuiteCRM system. It interacts with a database to handle job queue operations such as adding, fetching, resolving, and removing jobs, as well as cleaning up old or failed jobs.

classes.name: SugarJobQueue
classes.description: A class responsible for managing the job queue in SuiteCRM, including submitting, retrieving, resolving, deleting, and cleaning up scheduled jobs. It provides mechanisms to interact with the database to perform queue operations and maintains configuration settings for job retries and timeouts.

methods.name: __construct
methods.description: Initializes the job queue manager, setting up the database connection, determining the job queue table, and loading configuration settings for retries and timeouts.

methods.name: submitJob
methods.description: Submits a new job to the queue, assigning it a unique ID, default status, resolution, and execution time before saving it to the database.

methods.name: getJob
methods.description: Retrieves a job object from the database by its ID.

methods.name: resolveJob
methods.description: Marks a job as successfully completed or failed based on the provided resolution.

methods.name: postponeJob
methods.description: Reruns a job after a delay, optionally with a message.

methods.name: deleteJob
methods.description: Deletes a job from the queue by marking it as deleted.

methods.name: cleanup
methods.description: Forcefully marks running jobs that have exceeded the timeout as failed.

methods.name: clearHistoricJobs
methods.description: Deletes old successful and failed jobs based on their age thresholds.

methods.name: cleanQueue
methods.description: Removes all jobs from the queue, effectively emptying it.

methods.name: nextJob
methods.description: Fetches the next queued job and marks it as running, handling concurrent access via database updates.

methods.name: runSchedulers
methods.description: Triggers the schedulers to instantiate scheduled jobs.
